pages.title: Overview: Linked Lists
blocks: Linked Lists

A linked list stores a sequence of elements in nodes connected by references. This overview introduces singly and doubly linked lists, traversal, insertion, deletion, and the tradeoffs compared with arrays. Each node stores data and a reference to the next node.

pages.title: LEC28: Doubly Linked Lists Posted!

blocks: Program 7

pages.title: LLM: Linked Lists
blocks: Practice Prompts

pages.title: Overview: Recursion
blocks: Recursion

A recursive method calls itself on a smaller problem until a base case is reached. Trace the call stack to understand how each call returns. The Fibonacci sequence and factorial illustrate recursive decomposition.

pages.title: Binary Search
blocks: Searching Sorted Arrays
Binary search repeatedly halves the search interval in a sorted array. Its worst case running time is O(log n). Linear search checks each element and takes O(n) time.

pages.title: Stacks
blocks: Stack Operations
A stack removes the most recently added item first. This last in first out structure uses push to insert and pop to remove. An undo history can be implemented with a stack.

pages.title: Queues
blocks: Queue Operations
A queue removes the earliest added item first. This first in first out structure uses enqueue and dequeue. A printer job scheduler is a typical example.

pages.title: Iterators
blocks: Iterating Over Collections
An iterator visits collection elements without exposing the internal representation. The hasNext method checks whether another element exists; next returns that element.

pages.title: Exception Handling
blocks: Handling Errors
Use try and catch to handle exceptions without terminating the entire Java application. A finally block runs after the try and catch blocks to clean up resources.

pages.title: Generics
blocks: Generic Types
Java generics let one class work with different element types while preserving compile time type safety. Use a type parameter such as T rather than casting every stored Object.

pages.title: Inheritance
blocks: Extending Classes
A subclass inherits fields and methods from a superclass. Use extends to declare the relationship. Overriding a method changes its behavior for instances of the subclass.

pages.title: Binary Search Trees
blocks: Ordered Trees
Each node in a binary search tree has at most two children. Keys in the left subtree are smaller and keys in the right subtree are larger. Inorder traversal visits keys in sorted order.

pages.title: Arrays
blocks: Array Storage
An array stores elements in consecutive indexed slots and provides constant time access by index. Its length is fixed after allocation, unlike a linked structure that grows by adding nodes.

pages.title: Sorting Algorithms
blocks: Merge Sort
Merge sort divides the input into halves, sorts them recursively, and merges the sorted halves. Its worst case time complexity is O(n log n).

pages.title: Null References
blocks: NullPointerException
A NullPointerException occurs when code tries to access a field or call a method through a null reference. Check whether an object exists before dereferencing it.

pages.title: Polymorphism
blocks: Dynamic Dispatch
A superclass reference can point to a subclass instance. The overridden instance method called at runtime depends on the actual object type, not just the reference declaration.
